questions.stem: A heuristic returns a plan worth 81,200. The LP relaxation gives 82,900, and a MIP search stopped after 500 nodes reports a best bound of 81,900. What gap should the report state?

options.text: 0.86%, from the 81,900 bound, the tighter of the two upper bounds known
options.says: Right: every bound caps the optimum, so the tightest one gives the honest, smallest gap: (81,900 - 81,200) / 81,200.

options.text: 2.09%, from the 82,900 bound, the LP relaxation being the bound to quote
options.says: The LP bound is valid but looser; the page reports against the best bound known, here the stopped search's.

options.text: 0.00%, from the 81,200 plan, the best plan the heuristic itself has seen
options.says: A heuristic plan carries no proof; the gap compares it with a bound, not with itself.

options.text: Held back until the proof: a gap is stated once the optimum is known
options.says: The page states each plan's gap to the best bound known before any proof, and checks it once the optimum is known.

origin.section: Every Heuristic Plan Is Reported Against the Best Bound Known

questions.stem: A rolling horizon with 3-year windows, keeping 1 year each, ends 3.9% below the best bound; with 5-year windows, keeping 2, it ends 0.8% below. What explains most of the difference?

options.text: Longer windows search more nodes, and the node count sets a plan's quality
options.says: The 3-year run used 441 nodes and the 5-year run 6,592, but more nodes do not explain the loss: the loss is what a short window cannot see.

options.text: Shorter windows see fewer later years, so they misjudge where money pays
options.says: Right: the end effect. A window cannot see the better uses of money and crews that come after it.

options.text: Shorter windows keep fewer years, so their plans break more budget rows
options.says: Every rolling-horizon plan on the page breaks no rule; budget rows stay in for every year.

options.text: Longer windows relax the crew rows, so their plans reuse crews in a year
options.says: No window relaxes a crew row; every plan was checked against every rule.

origin.section: A Rolling Horizon Plans a Few Years at a Time and Keeps Only the First Ones

questions.stem: An LNS loop on GridCap's medium plan frees one region's projects per step, solves each step to optimality, and gains almost nothing in eight steps. What change is most likely to help?

options.text: Give each region step a longer time limit for its own search
options.says: Each step was already solved to optimality; more time finds nothing more in the same neighborhood.

options.text: Start the same region steps from the rolling-horizon plan
options.says: The page's region steps started from the rolling-horizon plan and gained $37k.

options.text: Cycle through the four regions again for eight more steps
options.says: On the page, steps 5 to 8 free Ridge, Valley, Coast and Plains again and the plan stays at 216,709.

options.text: Step through runs of three years instead of one region each
options.says: Right: GridCap's budget and crew rows are by year, so freeing years frees the projects that compete; on the page this gained $1,819k.

origin.section: A Neighborhood Must Free Projects That Compete for the Same Money and Crews
